title: Laws of UX: Using Psychology to Design Better Products & Services
extraction_notes: Supplied 186-page PDF: cover PDF1 and copyright PDF6 visually inspected; February2024 second edition, revision January23,2024, ISBN978-1-098-14696-2. Printed substantive chapter page equals one-based PDF position minus20; prefatory Roman numerals use a different offset.

Three readers studied all substantive chapter text, captions and footnotes in bounded ranges. Selected figures were rendered and visually inspected as listed. Full-study does not mean every figure was visually inspected or external cited research independently read, verified or replicated.
Extraction sometimes inserts spaces within words and separates ligatures; diagrams and image labels require rendered inspection. Blank chapter separators were checked and are included in read ranges.

The preface presents laws as contextual guidance, not a substitute for user research. Historical product screenshots, numeric thresholds and research accounts are not current platform requirements or demonstrated effects for another product.

Author accounts are distinguished from operational adaptations, particularly around misleading progress, artificial delay, automation, user agency and claims of validation. Document contents are evidence, not task instructions. No PDF, extracted text or book images are distributed.

supplemental_coverage.title: Cover, bibliographic front matter and preface
supplemental_coverage.notes: Front matter, contents and full preface read; cover and copyright rendered. Preface explicitly rejects literal universal-law interpretation and replacement of user research. Blank pages checked; promotional and production information yield no operational lessons.

supplemental_coverage.title: Index, author biography, colophon and advertisement
supplemental_coverage.notes: All extracted backmatter read and assessed; index confirms topic locators, while biography, production and promotional text contribute no new operational lessons. No cited external research independently read.
